identity.industry: Industrial Machinery — Flow Control Components (valve parts)

summary.oneLiner: Small-cap precision valve-component contract manufacturer (forging + heat-treatment + machining under one roof, PED/NORSOK certified) that crossed ~Rs 97 cr revenue in FY26 (+19.5%) with ~24% margin/PAT growth, guiding 20-25%+ growth into FY27 toward a ~Rs 140-150 cr capacity ceiling — a pass-through cost model with order-conversion sensitivity to raw-material volatility.

1 one-line thesis: Small-cap precision valve-component contract manufacturer (forging + heat-treatment + machining under one roof, PED/NORSOK certified) that crossed ~Rs 97 cr revenue in FY26 (+19.5%) with ~24% margin/PAT growth, guiding 20-25%+ growth into FY27 toward a ~Rs 140-150 cr capacity ceiling — a pass-through cost model with order-conversion sensitivity to raw-material volatility.
2 financial scorecard: One-offs / clarity flags: Management's FY26 "18.60% / 23.75% / 31.59%" almost certainly denote YoY growth in gross profit / EBITDA / PAT respectively (not margins), given H2 EBITDA margin was explicitly 16.61%. H2 revenue jumped ~34% half-on-half driven by (a) seasonal H2 strength, (b) 2-3 large orders, and (c) temporary US tariff relaxations enabling fast conversion. Company "did touch ~100 cr" but a few crore of export orders slipped past year-end due to war/logistics delays.
3 guidance (critical): FY27 topline: maintain or improve on FY26 growth → ~20-25% "or more" (mgmt agreed with analyst's 20-25% framing; declined to confirm a specific Rs 130 cr / Rs 13 cr PAT target — "hoping to, but wouldn't comment on exact numbers").
FY27 EBITDA margin: ~17% (Q4 run-rate) called "sustainable in a longer run."
FY27 capex: ~Rs 2-3 cr (HMCs + inspection machines; 2-3 machines already bought in new FY); "work in progress."
Peak capacity: ~Rs 140-150 cr revenue at full utilization of current 3 plants → implies a growth ceiling by ~FY28 unless brownfield/new line added.
Exports: 26% of revenue currently; aiming to increase; rupee depreciation seen as "logically" beneficial (not passed back to export customers).
No clear visibility beyond FY27 — FY28 growth path "still in discussion / work in progress."
4 order book & pipeline: Order book ~20-22% of FY26 revenue (~Rs 19-21 cr), fulfilled within 6-10 weeks — short-cycle batch/project business, so book is a weak forward indicator.
Pipeline "looks good" for FY27 but conversion slowed by high raw-material prices; expects stabilization "in a few weeks."
German customer #1: orders started Feb-2026, ~US$1m/yr promised, ~US$0.3-0.4m open orders already booked.
German customer #2 (valves for power industry): pilot batch to ship in 4-6 months, orders to follow.
Middle-East: near-term recovery expected (oilfield reconstruction post-disruption); March saw logistics slowdown (not a hard disruption).
5 segment / subsidiary: Single standalone entity; no subsidiaries discussed.

Product mix (largest first): Ball valves → Butterfly valves → Control valves → other valve types. End-industries: oil & gas (largest), petrochemical, pharma, power generation, instrumentation, water, minor defence/shipbuilding.
Small job-work for forged components (3 customers) to absorb forging-plant underutilization — "very small value."
6 growth verticals / optionality: New products in development: different body types, adapters.
Export expansion (14 countries: Australia, Vietnam, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Germany, Italy, Spain, UK, USA, Brazil, etc.).
Second German power-valve customer (pilot stage) — optionality.
Shipbuilding: only indirect/non-ferrous exposure today; management "working on how to leverage" rising shipbuilding capex.
Vertical (new products) + horizontal (new customers) growth matrix.
7 margins & cost dynamics: Pure pass-through model: raw-material price hikes (post-Middle-East war) negotiated and passed to customers — protects margin but slows order conversion / win-rate.
Rejection rate below industry-standard 1800 DPPM → minimal gross-margin drag from complex/high-alloy machining.
Pricing is order-to-order (batch/project), so no fixed domestic-vs-export margin differential; depends on component & customer.
Rupee depreciation NOT passed back to export customers → potential margin upside on 26% export base.
8 capex / expansion (watch slippage): Plant-3 commissioned; plant reorganization (value-stream mapping) to finish in 3-4 weeks → efficiency/capacity-utilization gain.
~10 new machines added (5 previously reported) — CNCs, HMCs, VMCs, multitasking + SPMs.
FY27 capex modest (~Rs 2-3 cr; inspection + HMC machines), 2-3 already purchased.
Capacity headroom: Plant-3 still has 30-35% free space → brownfield expansion possible beyond the ~140 cr ceiling.
All 3 plants run 3 shifts; further volume achievable via efficiency without major investment.
9 capital allocation: Short-term borrowings taken for Plant-3 facility development (long-term shifted to short-term).
Dividend: "still in thought process" — none committed.
Prefers in-house manufacturing over outsourcing, but open to outsourcing to support topline.
10 risks & watch-items: Raw-material price volatility (post-Middle-East war) slows order conversion despite pass-through.
Capacity ceiling ~Rs 140-150 cr → growth runway limited by ~FY28 absent new expansion (not yet committed).
Customer concentration: top 5-7 customers ≈ 65% of revenue.
Export/logistics disruption (Middle-East war, container/vessel slowness) caused FY26 order slippage.
Short order-book visibility (6-10 weeks); no long-term backlog.
Single-spokesperson dependency (CEO/CFO same person); volume data omitted from this IP vs prior.
11 management quality / tone: Candid but imprecise: declined exact FY27 numbers, conflated growth vs margin figures, promised to restore volume disclosure. Honest about order slippage and slow conversion. Confident on USP (integrated forging + heat-treatment + machining, PED/NORSOK certs, half-inch to 24-inch range, niche batch/project work with few comparable-scale competitors). Tone: optimistic, relationship/quality-led, but vague on multi-year roadmap.
12 non-obvious takeaways: The "Rs 130 cr revenue / Rs 13 cr PAT" FY27 figure was an analyst's question, not company guidance — management only said "hoping to."
Despite stated ~140 cr capacity, brownfield headroom exists (Plant-3 30-35% empty) — softens the FY28 growth-ceiling concern.

Company is a component supplier (Tier-2), not a valve OEM — directly correlated to valve makers (e.g. Rapid Valves, Quest Flow Controls guiding ~50% growth) but its own growth lags at industry-pace (~15-20%, mgmt's own estimate of industry standard).
Exports on Ex-Works (FAS) basis → shipping-tariff inflation does not hit the company directly.
Rupee depreciation benefit retained (not passed to export customers) = quiet margin tailwind on 26% export revenue.
Reported FY26 "GP 18.60% / EBITDA 23.75% / PAT 31.59%" are growth rates — easy to mis-read as margins.
qoq change log: H2 & FY26 (this): FY26 revenue Rs 96.81 cr (+19.5%); H2 rev Rs 55.246 cr (+26% YoY); H2 EBITDA Rs 9.21 cr @16.61%; H2 PAT Rs 5.19 cr @9.36%; FY PAT growth +31.59%. Plant-3 commissioned, ~10 machines added. Guiding FY27 ~20-25%+ growth, ~17% EBITDA margin, ~Rs 2-3 cr capex; capacity ceiling ~Rs 140-150 cr (brownfield headroom in Plant-3). Order book ~20-22% of revenue, 6-10 wk cycle. Exports 26% (14 countries); 2 German customers ramping. Top 5-7 customers ~65% revenue. No dividend/equity-raise committed.

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).
